channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Marine
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Two confirmed tanker intrusions and an unverified LNG-carrier claim keep vessel control-system access in focus
item.description: The Coast Guard and FBI have confirmed intrusions by a foreign cyber actor on two US-bound tankers boarded in late August, including the Liberian-flagged crude tanker VL Prosperity. The Coast Guard reported no operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and CISA said the actors “did not appear to have taken control of the vessels themselves.” A third case is unconfirmed: the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG lost access to some internal control systems in early September while bound for the Adriatic with a Louisiana cargo, and diverted toward Spain (first reported by Bloomberg on 18 September). The crew’s claim that attackers seized pressure and safety-valve systems is unverified; Italy’s Coast Guard recorded a cargo-monitoring malfunction of undetermined cause. Bloomberg reports that nearly 20 ships are being tracked; no official figure has been published. On 24 September Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to “invest, test, monitor and strengthen our defenses now”; it reported no incident at any Texas operator. No attribution has been confirmed. - Bloomberg, 18 Sep 2026 (Vivit Africa LNG); Railroad Commission of Texas statement, 24 Sep 2026 (primary); Splash247, Cybernews, Dragos - Boardings 21 Aug 2026 and days later; Vivit Africa LNG incident early Sep 2026; no official development after 24 Sep

item.title: [High] Port of Tanjung Pelepas restarted in phases after a cyber incident halted container operations
item.description: A cyber incident detected shortly before midnight on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), a joint venture of MMC and Maersk’s APM Terminals, to suspend container terminal operations and its terminal operating systems as a precaution. A phased restart began on 10 September, initially with manual processing for export container gate-ins, and a PTP spokesperson said on 15 September that operations had resumed with system recovery “advancing steadily.” Maersk called it a cybersecurity incident and said it had no evidence customer data was accessed. The Direwolf ransomware group listed the port on its leak site on 11 September, claiming 200 GB of data (per ransomware.live); PTP has not confirmed ransomware or any group, so that remains a claim. No new development reported as of 27 September. - PTP spokesperson via WorldCargo News, 15 Sep 2026 (primary); The Loadstar, 11 Sep; Direwolf listing via ransomware.live, 11 Sep (claim) - Incident 9 Sep 2026; phased restart from 10 Sep; operations resumed per 15 Sep statement

item.title: [Medium] Port of Los Angeles says it blocked more than 120 million attempted cyberattacks in August
item.category: Context — Attempted attacks against a major port
item.description: Port of Los Angeles Executive Director Gene Seroka told Bloomberg Television on 17 September that the port blocked more than 120 million attempted cyberattacks in August, citing intrusion attempts, network exploitation, credential harvesting and malware. These were blocked attempts, not successful intrusions, and the port has not reported any compromise of terminal systems. The figure measures the volume of probing a major port absorbs, not the risk to any one terminal. - Gene Seroka on Bloomberg TV, 17 Sep 2026 (primary); Transport Topics - Reporting period: August 2026; published 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Secure FMC, a common firewall console at IT/OT boundaries, remains under active exploitation
item.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco Talos tracks three clusters exploiting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center flaws. UAT-12197 used CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated root) to plant web shells. UAT-11823, an APT whose tooling overlaps with Sandworm’s and which deployed a Cyclops Blink variant, used both CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator, deployed Qilin after logging in with the CVE-2026-20316 static credentials. Talos names no victims, sectors or countries, and there has been no new development since its 21 September update. Editorial assessment: FMC often manages the firewalls between corporate IT and terminal operating systems, crane and gate networks at ports. - Cisco Talos analysis, 9 Sep 2026, updated 21 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV entry 9 Sep 2026 - Exploitation confirmed 9 Sep 2026; Talos update 21 Sep 2026; no new development as of 27 Sep

item.title: [High] Forescout: only 13% of network segments containing OT devices are OT-only
item.description: Forescout’s Vedere Labs analysed 47,700 network segments holding more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations (published 22 September; reported by Industrial Cyber 24 September). Only 13% of segments containing OT devices were OT-only; the rest held other device types, and almost half mixed OT with both IT and IoT assets. Editorial assessment: aboard vessels and at terminals, where crew Wi-Fi, cargo systems and navigation networks increasingly share infrastructure, this is the architectural gap that lets one compromised laptop or crew device reach navigation or cargo-control systems. - Forescout Vedere Labs research (22 Sep 2026), reported by Industrial Cyber, 24 Sep 2026 - Published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Anthropic: an Iran-linked actor used its AI model to track US Navy vessels and research maritime VSAT flaws
item.description: Anthropic reported on about 11 September that an Iran-linked actor used its Claude model to build a Python OSINT pipeline for identifying and tracking US Navy vessel positions, compiling “targeting handbooks” with personnel rosters, ship and aircraft transponder identifiers and satellite-imagery scripts. The actor also compiled vulnerability data on maritime VSAT terminals, Cisco communications equipment and industrial control products. Anthropic banned the account and shared intelligence with government authorities. The targets were naval, not commercial shipping, and the report describes reconnaissance and research use, not intrusion into any vessel. No new development reported as of 27 September. - Anthropic threat report, ~11 Sep 2026, via gCaptain and Navy Times (11 Sep 2026) - Reported 11 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] watchTowr: two unpatched NetScaler RCE zero-days are being exploited; Citrix has not yet confirmed
item.category: Advisory — Unpatched remote-access zero-days, vendor unconfirmed
item.description: watchTowr said on 26 September that two distinct remote-code-execution flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway are being exploited in the wild, discovered during forensic investigations. As of the morning of 27 September, Citrix (Cloud Software Group) had published no advisory, CVE, affected-build list, indicators or fix; outlets report fixes are expected the week of 28 September. watchTowr says these are not CVE-2026-19490, August’s authentication bypass, and it is not yet known whether the August builds protect against them. NetScaler 13.1 reached end of maintenance on 15 September. Shutdown advice circulating from IT suppliers cites a private briefing; watchTowr did not recommend shutdown and there is no public NCSC-NL advisory. Editorial assessment: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into port, terminal and OT DMZ networks. - watchTowr statements, 26 Sep 2026 (primary); The Hacker News, 27 Sep 2026 - Reported 26 Sep 2026; no vendor advisory as of 27 Sep

item.title: [High] Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard hard-coded keys: CISA update rates both flaws 8.3 and names the fixed build
item.category: Advisory — Hard-coded cryptographic keys, fix available, no known exploitation
item.description: CISA’s ICSA-26-258-02 (15 September; Update A, 24 September) covers two hard-coded cryptographic key flaws (CWE-321) in Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard 5.07.0923.01, a shipboard fleet-optimization system: CVE-2026-81855 in its robot testing framework and CVE-2026-78225 in its deployer-ng Update Controller. Both are rated CVSS 8.3 with an adjacent-network attack vector, so an attacker needs access to the same local network. Update A adds the fixed version, 5.08.4052.01. A hard-coded key is shared by every installation, so a key recovered from one vessel can work across the fleet. No exploitation has been reported. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-258-02, 15 Sep 2026; Update A, 24 Sep 2026 (primary) - Fixed version published 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI name transportation among sectors exposed through a compromised ICS integrator
item.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator remote access
item.description: A joint FBI/CISA fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators” (dated 23 September, publicised 24 September), describes foreign cyber actors who compromised a US industrial automation company in March–April 2025 and staged customer SCADA data, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration. It names power utilities and transportation entities among the affected customers. It recommends security terms in integrator contracts, least privilege, less internet exposure, and integrator remote access through monitored, logged, on-demand paths. Editorial assessment: shipyards, OEMs and other service providers often hold standing remote access to vessel and terminal control systems, so this applies directly to marine operators. - FBI/CISA fact sheet, dated 23 Sep 2026, published 24 Sep 2026 (primary) - Cites a March–April 2025 intrusion at a US automation integrator

item.title: [Info] Coast Guard announces a dedicated Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy
item.category: Policy — New Coast Guard maritime cybersecurity office
item.description: The US Coast Guard announced on 31 August that it has established an Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy under the Director of Inspections and Compliance (CG-5PC). It arrives as the Coast Guard’s MTSA cybersecurity rule phases in: cyber incidents have been reportable to the National Response Center since July 2025, and owners and operators need a designated Cybersecurity Officer, a cybersecurity assessment and an approved plan by 16 July 2027 (per Dragos’ 24 September summary of the rule). - US Coast Guard Maritime Commons, 31 Aug 2026 (primary); SecurityWeek - Announced 31 Aug 2026
